name: Can you keep a bathtub somewhere else if you remove the only tub in the house?

mainEntity.name: If the only bathtub is removed, can the home still work well for resale or family use?
mainEntity.text: If the only bathtub is removed, can the home still work well for resale or family use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removing the only bathtub can be a smart upgrade for some households, but it is not always the best resale decision. Families with young children often value at least one tub in the home, while many adults prefer a larger, easier-to-enter shower. In Los Angeles-area neighborhoods, the right choice depends on the property type, number of bathrooms, and target buyer profile. If the home has multiple bathrooms, keeping one tub elsewhere can preserve flexibility. If there is only one bathroom, homeowners should think carefully before eliminating the tub entirely. The best approach is to match the remodel to how the home is actually used, not just current design trends. A conversion can still be a good investment if it improves accessibility, opens up space, or modernizes a badly dated bath. Before deciding, consider who uses the home now, who might buy it later, and whether the remaining bathrooms cover the household’s needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but it depends on the home’s layout and buyer expectations. In family homes, removing the only bathtub can reduce flexibility, while in some markets a well-designed shower may be preferred. Many owners keep at least one tub elsewhere if possible.
